title: Sausage, pork, chorizo, link or ground, cooked, pan-fried

content.title: About
content.content: Pork chorizo sausage is a flavorful, slightly spicy sausage made from ground pork, spices, and salt, then pan‑fried until a golden crust forms. It is a staple in Mexican and Spanish cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chorizo originates from Spanish cuisine, where it is made both fresh and cured.
Traditional recipes include paprika, garlic, and red pepper, giving it its characteristic color and aroma.
Regional variations may add wine vinegar, dried herbs, or even cheese.
Chorizo is commonly used in paella, beans, omelets, and pasta dishes.
The pork blend often contains both lean meat and fat, keeping the sausage juicy.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Pork provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B1, B3, B6, and B12, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron helps maintain hemoglobin levels and prevents anemia.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune health and wound healing.

items.title: Energy‑dense fats
items.content: Moderate fat content provides a concentrated energy source and aids absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: The salt used in processing can raise blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Saturated fat content should be moderated, especially for individuals with cardiovascular concerns.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to pork.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Commercial versions may contain nitrites and other preservatives that should be limited.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chorizo can be pan‑fried, added to stews, pasta, omelets, tacos, soups, or used as a pizza topping. When pan‑frying, a hot dry skillet works well because the sausage already contains fat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0–4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container for 3–5 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 2 months.
